## Defender notes by technique

| Technique | Hardening control | IR step | Risk treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1003.002 | Remove standing local admin rights, randomise local admin passwords with LAPS, and alert on reg save of the SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives. | Isolate the host, treat local and cached credentials as compromised and reset them, and preserve the saved hive files as evidence. | Mitigate: LAPS and least privilege reduce the value of dumped hashes; accept residual risk for documented backup tooling via the filter. |
| T1012 | Collect process-creation events with full command lines and baseline legitimate registry query tooling per host role. | Review the parent process chain and the same user's session for follow-on discovery or credential access. | Accept: low-impact discovery on its own; monitor and escalate when combined with other discovery or execution alerts. |
| T1016 | Log DNS queries centrally and baseline which processes legitimately contact connectivity-check domains. | Identify the querying process and its parent, then check for proxy or C2 behaviour from the same host. | Accept: network configuration discovery is common noise; tune thresholds and keep the alert as a correlation signal. |
| T1016.001 | Log command lines for cmd.exe children and restrict network utilities that standard users do not need. | Determine what launched cmd.exe, review commands run in the same session, and check outbound connections afterwards. | Accept with monitoring: connectivity checks are frequently benign; escalate only with other attacker behaviour. |
| T1018 | Segment workstations from server networks and log net.exe usage with command lines. | Identify the account and host, review which systems were enumerated, and look for follow-on lateral movement. | Mitigate: segmentation limits what enumeration reveals; accept the residual discovery noise. |
| T1021.001 | Restrict RDP to a jump host or VPN, require MFA for remote access, and enable Network Level Authentication. | Contain the source and destination hosts, disable the used account, and review the RDP session logs for actions taken. | Mitigate: MFA and network restrictions on RDP; transfer residual risk for third-party access via contract controls. |
| T1021.002 | Block SMB between workstations with host firewalls, disable SMBv1, and require SMB signing and encryption. | Isolate the source host, identify mapped shares and files accessed, and reset credentials used for the mapping. | Mitigate: host firewall and signing controls; accept the residual risk on file servers that must expose SMB. |
| T1033 | Collect command-line audit logs and restrict scripting engines to users who need them. | Check what spawned the scripting engine and whether it ran with user or elevated rights, then widen to the host timeline. | Accept: owner discovery is low-impact; the alert is valuable mostly as correlation context. |
| T1036.005 | Enforce application allowlisting so system utilities only run from their expected paths, and alert on path mismatches. | Hash and preserve the masquerading binary, compare it to the legitimate file, and hunt for the same hash across hosts. | Mitigate: allowlisting; accept residual risk where admins run copies of tools from non-standard paths. |
| T1046 | Deploy network intrusion detection, collect flow logs, and keep externally exposed services to the minimum. | Block or rate-limit the scanning source, confirm which services responded, and prioritise patching of exposed ones. | Accept: internet scanning is constant background noise; mitigate by reducing exposed attack surface. |
| T1048.003 | Use egress filtering with an allowlist, inspect outbound HTTP at the proxy, and deploy data loss prevention for sensitive stores. | Contain the host, identify the destination and data volume sent, and start breach assessment and notification decisions. | Mitigate: egress control and DLP; for confirmed loss, treat as a reportable incident and involve legal. |
| T1049 | Log command lines for chained cmd.exe commands and restrict netstat-style tooling for standard users where practical. | Review the chained commands and parent process, then check for connections to unusual hosts from the same machine. | Accept: connection discovery is common; use as a correlation signal. |
| T1053.005 | Restrict scheduled task creation to administrators and alert on logon or startup triggered tasks created from user context. | Export the task definition, identify the action it runs, delete it once preserved, and hunt for the same task name elsewhere. | Mitigate: least privilege on task creation; accept the residual risk for approved software installers. |
| T1055 | Enable anti-exploitation features and behaviour-based EDR, and constrain PowerShell with Constrained Language Mode and script block logging. | Isolate the host, capture memory of the injected process, and identify the payload source URL for blocking. | Mitigate: EDR and PowerShell constraints; residual risk accepted for unmanaged developer machines with compensating monitoring. |
| T1057 | Collect command-line audit logs and restrict scripting engines for users who do not need them. | Check the scripting engine's parent and the rest of its session for credential or lateral movement activity. | Accept: process discovery is low-impact; escalate only with other attacker behaviour. |
| T1059.001 | Enable PowerShell script block and module logging, apply Constrained Language Mode, and allowlist approved scripts. | Collect script block logs, identify the download source and parent process, and quarantine any written files. | Mitigate: logging and language constraints; accept residual risk for administrators who need full PowerShell. |
| T1059.003 | Allowlist approved scripts, restrict cmd.exe and batch execution from user-writable paths, and log command lines. | Retrieve the batch file, review its contents, and trace its origin (download, email or share) before deletion. | Mitigate: script allowlisting; accept residual risk from legitimate admin automation. |
| T1069.002 | Review privileged group membership regularly, apply role-based access control, and log net.exe group enumeration. | Identify the account and host, review which groups were enumerated, and watch that account for privilege escalation. | Mitigate: tidy privileged groups to reduce what enumeration reveals; accept discovery noise. |
| T1082 | Collect command-line audit logs and baseline legitimate inventory tooling. | Check the parent process and subsequent commands in the session; treat as reconnaissance and widen the hunt. | Accept: system discovery is low-impact and common; use for correlation. |
| T1083 | Apply least-privilege file ACLs so recursive enumeration yields little, and log command lines. | Identify the directories enumerated, check for staging or archive activity next, and review the account's recent file access. | Accept with monitoring: file discovery is normal user behaviour; escalate when followed by archiving or exfiltration. |
| T1087.001 | Maintain an account inventory, disable dormant local accounts, and log whoami and account enumeration commands. | Check the scripting parent and the rest of the session, and confirm the account used is legitimate. | Accept: local account discovery is low-impact; escalate in combination with credential access. |
| T1105 | Filter outbound web access with a URL allowlist or proxy and block direct PowerShell downloads from untrusted hosts. | Retrieve and hash the downloaded file, block the source URL, and scan for execution of the payload. | Mitigate: egress filtering; accept residual risk for approved software update paths. |
| T1110.001 | Enforce account lockout, require MFA, ban weak passwords, and restrict net use to administrators. | Identify the targeted accounts and share, reset any account that may have succeeded, and block the source. | Mitigate: lockout and MFA; accept residual risk for legacy systems that cannot enforce MFA, with compensating monitoring. |
| T1112 | Enforce secure configuration baselines through Group Policy and restrict reg.exe for standard users. | Record the key and value changed, revert it to baseline, and determine what process and user made the change. | Mitigate: configuration management; accept low-impact cosmetic changes with monitoring. |
| T1204.002 | Block macros from internet-sourced Office files, filter risky attachment types, and run phishing awareness training. | Isolate the host, retrieve the document and macro, identify the delivery email, and purge it from other mailboxes. | Mitigate: macro blocking and training; transfer part of the risk with email security services. |
| T1216 | Use application control to restrict signed proxy-execution binaries and scripts to approved uses. | Identify the proxied payload, preserve the MSI or script, and scope its install or execution footprint. | Mitigate: application control; accept residual risk for legitimate software deployment tools. |
| T1218.007 | Restrict msiexec to administrators or software distribution, block installs from user-writable paths, and apply application control. | Retrieve the MSI package, inspect its custom actions, and uninstall and remove artefacts after scoping. | Mitigate: application control; accept residual risk for approved silent deployments. |
| T1482 | Restrict directory trust enumeration to administrative accounts and log net.exe command chains. | Identify the account and host, review the trusts enumerated, and watch for cross-domain lateral movement. | Accept with monitoring: trust discovery is rare for standard users and valuable as a high-signal indicator. |
| T1546.011 | Disable application compatibility shim installation for standard users and audit AppCompatFlags registry changes. | Export the shim database and registry keys, remove the registration, and check the shimmed application for tampering. | Mitigate: configuration control; accept residual risk for legitimate compatibility fixes with change approval. |
| T1555.004 | Restrict cmdkey use, enable Credential Guard, and prefer MFA over stored RDP credentials. | Identify the stored credentials and targets, reset affected accounts, and review RDP connections that followed. | Mitigate: Credential Guard and MFA; accept residual risk for legitimate stored administrator sessions. |
| T1560.001 | Restrict archive utilities on sensitive systems, apply DLP, and monitor staging directories. | Locate and preserve the archive, identify what data it contains, and check for exfiltration from the same host. | Mitigate: DLP; accept noise from legitimate compression, escalating when paired with outbound transfer. |
| T1564.001 | Enforce Explorer settings (show file extensions) through Group Policy and restrict reg.exe for standard users. | Revert the value, look for files using double extensions, and trace the delivery of those files. | Mitigate: configuration management; the change itself is low-impact, so accept with monitoring. |
| T1569.002 | Disable unnecessary services, restrict service creation to administrators, and baseline svchost service groups. | Inspect the new or modified service binary and parameters, preserve it, and remove persistence once scoped. | Mitigate: service allowlisting and least privilege; accept residual risk from legitimate administrative tooling. |
| T1614.001 | Collect command-line audit logs and baseline legitimate regional and language queries. | Check the process chain for malware that tailors its behaviour to locale, and hunt for follow-on execution. | Accept: language discovery is low-impact alone; treat as a correlation signal. |
